reason: E2 states that electrospark deposition with argon produces coatings with low oxygen concentration, and that HEA coatings can enhance corrosion resistance without major impact on the workpiece, supporting the barrier and minimal mechanical impact premises. However, no cited evidence addresses the retention of the substrate's specific mechanical properties (tensile ductility, yield strength) or the coating's performance at 1000 °C, leaving those key premises unsupported.
premises: Electrospark deposition can produce a HfNbTaTiZr coating with low oxygen content due to argon shielding
HEA coatings can enhance corrosion resistance without major impact on the workpiece
The coating will act as an oxygen barrier, reducing oxidation of the underlying alloy
The underlying cast HfNbTaTiZr will retain its mechanical properties (ductility, yield strength) after coating
The coating will remain effective and mechanically stable up to 1000 °C under inert gas
